records.name_note: Three admissible sources structure the name differently and split on which name leads. NC State's Common Name(s) field is an alphabetized stacked list -- Early Sunflower, Eastern Ox-eye, Eastern Sunflower-everlasting, False Sunflower, Heliopsis, Ox-eye, Oxeye Sunflower, Smooth Oxeye -- designating no primary entry; its own body prose instead opens 'Oxeye sunflower or false sunflower is a native, herbaceous perennial...', leading with Oxeye sunflower. MoBoT shows an affirmative 'Common Name: oxeye sunflower' field whose attached Common Names list reads 'oxeye sunflower, smooth oxeye' in that order and omits 'false sunflower' altogether; its species prose likewise opens 'Heliopsis helianthoides, commonly called oxeye sunflower or ox-eye daisy'; only its genus-level prose adds that 'Heliopsis is sometimes commonly called false sunflower.' RHS's H1 is the bare binomial, with 'smooth ox-eye' as the plant-profile subtitle and 'North American ox-eye' under its separate Other common names field; the strings 'oxeye sunflower' and 'false sunflower' do not appear on the RHS page at all. Two of the three sources' primacy signals point to Oxeye sunflower and one (RHS) points to smooth ox-eye, so Oxeye Sunflower is used here; 'False Sunflower' (the app's search term) never leads on any of the three.
unknowns: is_houseplant: none of the three admissible sources (NC State, MoBoT, RHS) address whether this species is grown as a houseplant; all three treat it exclusively as an outdoor garden/meadow perennial, so left null rather than inferred.

toxic_to_pets / toxicity_detail: none of the three admissible sources' pages for this species carry any Poison, toxicity, or pet-safety information -- NC State's page has no Poison / Problem-for-Cats / Problem-for-Dogs block at all, MoBoT's Problems section covers only insects, disease, and staking, and RHS's page has no toxicity statement. Left null per the rule against inferring toxicity from general plant/genus knowledge.

chill_damage_f, cool_rest_note, day_f_min/max, night_f_min/max, humidity_need, humidity_pct_min/max, light_fc_min/good: no admissible source gives a numeric damage-onset temperature, day/night temperature range, humidity target, or foot-candle light figure for this outdoor perennial; RHS's H6 hardiness rating is a survival/zone rating, not a damage-onset temperature, so it was not used for chill_damage_f.

direct_sun_hours_max: NC State's '6 or more hours of direct sunlight a day' text appears only inside its site-wide Light-category legend (attached to the generic 'Full sun' tag used across all plant pages), not in species-specific prose about this plant, so per the rules it was excluded and left null.

outdoor_sun_exposure: NC State's structured Light field additionally lists 'Partial Shade (Direct sunlight only part of the day, 2-6 hours)', but MoBoT's structured Sun field and RHS's structured Position field both list only Full sun. Per the rule that a value excluded by two of three sources' structured sun fields is left out, part_shade/part_sun was omitted from outdoor_sun_exposure even though NC State's structured field and its 'partial shade tolerant' tag support it.

soil_ph_min/soil_ph_max: NC State lists open-ended 'Acid (<6.0)' and closed 'Neutral (6.0-8.0)' bands. RHS's Cultivation pH field states soils are accepted as 'Acid, alkaline, or neutral,' i.e. RHS explicitly accepts alkaline soil, so per the rule the Neutral band's 8.0 ceiling cannot be used and soil_ph_max is left null; because NC State's own Acid band is open below 6.0 (no floor stated) and RHS also accepts acid soils, soil_ph_min is left null as well.

water_regime: no admissible source frames watering as a directive statement matching one of the four enum categories. MoBoT's structured field reads 'Water: Dry to medium' -- a mid/dry-scale data point disclosed here as a counterpoint rather than used to populate the enum -- and both MoBoT's and NC State's prose describe soil-moisture tolerance and drought tolerance ('Tolerates drought, but does best if regularly watered'; soil 'medium moist to dry and well-drained') rather than giving a watering instruction, so water_regime was left null.

water_dry_down_target, water_check_depth_cm, water_growing_days_est, water_dormant_days_est, water_estimate_basis: this is an in-ground garden perennial and no admissible source frames its watering in dry-down, check-depth, or day-interval terms, so per the rules these were left null rather than estimated.
fertilize_interval_days, fertilize_active_months, fertilize_strength: none of the three admissible sources give any fertilizing guidance for this species, so all fertilize_* fields were left null.

soil_base: no admissible source uses container/soil-mix language (e.g. potting mix, cactus mix); garden_bed was chosen because all three sources consistently describe the plant only as an in-ground perennial for borders, cottage gardens, meadows, and naturalized/prairie plantings, never as a container or indoor plant.

records.name_note: All four admissible sources use Swamp Milkweed in prose, and all three sources carrying a structured common-name field designate it, but each source structures its common names differently. NC State's Common Name(s) field is an alphabetized stacked list (Marsh Milkweed, Swamp Butterfly Weed, Swamp Milkweed) marking no entry as primary -- the alphabetically-first "Marsh Milkweed" is an ordering artifact, not NC State's preferred name, and its page title carries the same parenthetical in the same order; NC State's own Description prose instead opens "Swamp milkweed is an herbaceous perennial...", showing that is the name NC State itself uses. MoBoT's page carries an affirmative "Common Name: swamp milkweed" field (a primacy designation), with a longer Common Names list ("swamp milkweed", "water nerveroot") behind a tooltip. RHS's H1 is the bare binomial Asclepias incarnata; "swamp milkweed" is rendered directly beneath it as the plant-profile subtitle, and separately appears in the page title as "Asclepias incarnata | swamp milkweed", with "water nerveroot" listed separately under Other common names. Penn State Extension's dedicated article is titled "Rain Garden Plants: Swamp Milkweed" and opens "Swamp milkweed is a showy perennial...". "Water nerveroot" appears as a secondary/alternate name on both MoBoT and RHS but never as the lead name on any admissible page, and NC State does not list it at all.
records.toxicity_detail: NC State Extension's Poison block (human-scoped) rates Poison Severity as "Low," with Poison Symptoms: "Can cause stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhea, weakness, lethargy, and confusion if eaten in quantity. Milky sap can cause contact dermatitis and eye irritation" Poison Toxic Principle is "Cardiac glycosides and resinoids." The Poison Part list, reproduced in full, is Flowers, Fruits, Leaves, Roots, Seeds, Stems -- essentially the whole plant. NC State also tags the plant "Poisonous" as a Whole Plant Trait, lists "Contact Dermatitis" and "Poisonous to Humans" among its Problems alongside the Problem for Cats/Dogs/Horses tags, and answers its own "Causes Contact Dermatitis" field "Yes" -- so gloves are warranted when cutting or handling stems, independent of the ingestion risk. Separately from that human-scoped Poison block, NC State's own structured plant tags include "Problem for Cats" and "Problem for Dogs" (as well as "Problem for Horses," which is outside this app's cat/dog scope), which is the basis for flagging this species as toxic to cats and dogs specifically.
unknowns: soil_ph_min and soil_ph_max are left null: NC State's Soil pH tags span the Acid (<6.0) band (open-ended low, so no floor) plus the Neutral (6.0-8.0) band (closed top of 8.0, a candidate ceiling), but RHS's pH field for this species explicitly lists 'Acid or Alkaline or Neutral' -- since RHS accepts alkaline soils, the candidate 8.0 ceiling from NC State's Neutral band is not adopted and soil_ph_max stays null; soil_ph_min stays null because NC State's own Acid band is open-ended.

water_regime is set to keep_moist on Penn State Extension's structured Hydrologic zone field ('Wet/moist; occasional flooding'). MoBoT's own structured Water field reads 'Medium to wet,' a more mid-scale value that is disclosed as a counterpoint rather than adopted; NC State's habitat prose ('native to wet sites but adapts to drier sites') was not used for water_regime because it describes wild habitat/drought tolerance rather than a watering statement.

outdoor_sun_exposure includes full_sun and part_shade based on NC State's Light field and Penn State Extension's Sun field, both of which list sun and partial shade unconditionally. RHS's Position field and MoBoT's Sun field list Full sun only, with no partial-shade value on either -- that split (2 sources for, 2 sources against part_shade) is disclosed here since it does not cleanly satisfy either side of the majority rule for excluding a value.

direct_sun_hours_max and light_fc_min/light_fc_good are left null: NC State's only hour figures ('6 or more hours' for full sun, '2-6 hours' for partial shade) come from its site-wide light-category legend, not species-specific prose, and no admissible source gives a foot-candle light value for this species.

chill_damage_f and cool_rest_note are left null: no admissible source states a numeric damage-onset temperature for this species; only USDA hardiness-zone ranges (NC State 3a-9b, MoBoT zone 3 to 6/7, RHS H4) were found, and those are zone/survival ratings, not onset figures.

day_f_min/max, night_f_min/max, humidity_need, humidity_pct_min/max, and all fertilize_* fields are left null: no admissible source addresses daytime/nighttime temperature targets, ambient humidity, or fertilizing for this species.

water_dry_down_target, water_check_depth_cm, water_growing_days_est, water_dormant_days_est, and water_estimate_basis are left null per the task's own instruction to leave these null for an in-ground perennial unless a source frames watering that way -- none of the admissible sources give a numeric watering-interval or dry-down-depth framing for this species.

UF/IFAS (ask.ifas.ufl.edu / edis.ifas.ufl.edu) admissible-domain search results only turned up passing mentions of swamp milkweed as a monarch host plant and a late-season landscape companion, with no species-specific cultural or toxicity detail usable for any schema field, so no UF/IFAS citation was included.
